headline: Government Raya Open Houses Cancelled: Modest Savings, Real Trade-offs
context: On 11 March 2026 Cabinet ordered government agencies, GLCs and GLICs to cancel Hari Raya open houses and capped minister travel as cost moderation. MOF put fuel subsidies at up to RM4B a month on 26 March and about RM7B on 15 April.

changes.summary: Correction: The order covered government agencies, GLCs and GLICs, not all open houses. The RM15 million to RM25 million is now reported as lost private revenue. Qualified an unverified claim about women-led catering.

Correction: MOF's fuel-subsidy estimate was about RM7B a month by 15 April, not RM4B. Two claims that lacked two independent sources, and three unsourced figures (RM15-25M lost revenue, 50-60% catering share, DOSM women-owned F&B), were dropped or replaced with sourced text.

cards.big: Government open houses are off this Raya. The savings sit beside a fuel-subsidy bill MOF put at about RM7 billion a month.
cards.sub: The order covers government agencies, GLCs and GLICs, not all open houses in Malaysia. Private and household events are not in scope.

cards.big: A Dewan Rakyat reply said the 2013 PM and Cabinet open house at Seri Perdana drew over 80,000 guests.
cards.sub: Official open houses are taxpayer-funded: that event's food and drink cost RM2.88M, about RM36 a guest. Scale and procurement vary by year and host.

cards.big: World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur's group CEO told Bernama the cancellation 'does have an impact on industry players like us'. He gave no figure.
cards.sub: He urged events firms to diversify beyond big seasonal events and 'be ready to pivot quickly'.

cards.big: Indonesia's president still held a palace open house for Eid al-Fitr 2026. Malaysia chose a full ban for the agencies, GLCs and GLICs named.
cards.sub: The PMO framed it as spending moderation. Whether that signal lands depends on whether other government cost lines move proportionally.

cards.big: The question is not whether to host this year. It is whether procurement for official open houses is transparent enough to scale them without scrapping them.
Symbolic austerity is real signalling, but small in fiscal terms. A durable answer is published procurement and audited costs for official festive events, not an on-off switch.
